title: api: unify rate-limit semantics, idempotency keys & retry-after; strengthen OpenAI compat error codes
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: customers and SDKs observed inconsistent behavior across our API surface when requests hit capacity or transient backends: (1) inconsistent Retry-After headers (seconds vs HTTP-date), (2) different error bodies between hosted endpoints and the OpenAI compatibility layer, (3) streaming connections that dropped silently when rate limits were enforced, and (4) unclear idempotency semantics leading to duplicate side-effects. This PR consolidates server-side semantics for rate limiting and idempotency, normalizes Retry-After handling, and strengthens the OpenAI compatibility error mapping so downstream SDKs can rely on consistent codes and structured error fields.

What this changes (summary):
- Standardize rate-limit responses: always return HTTP 429 with structured JSON body {"type":"rate_limit","code":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"...","retry_after":"<seconds>"} and include a Retry-After header. Retry-After is emitted as an integer number of seconds when we can estimate backoff, otherwise as an HTTP-date per spec.
- OpenAI compatibility layer: map internal error families to a stable set of OpenAI-like error codes and types so third-party SDKs that inspect error.type / error.code behave consistently. Add missing fields (param, internal_context) to the compat response.
- Idempotency keys: introduce X-Idempotency-Key middleware for POST endpoints that mutate state (deployments, model uploads, billing events). Behavior: first request is processed normally; subsequent requests with the same key and identical body return the stored result (200/201), mismatched bodies return 409 with structured error code idempotency_conflict. We persist idempotency records for 24 hours by default.
- Retry-After semantics for streaming: streaming endpoints now emit a final structured error event over the stream (type=rate_limit) instead of abruptly closing the connection. This allows clients to surface a stable error and follow Retry-After; a Retry-After header is sent at stream start when immediate rate-limiting is the case.
- SDK and docs updates: small compatibility layers in openai_compat.py and redwood-js mapping; docs page on rate-limits and idempotency added.

Checklist: 
- [x] Standardize JSON error envelope across REST and streaming.
- [x] Implement X-Idempotency-Key middleware and store.
- [x] Ensure Retry-After header is emitted consistently (seconds or HTTP-date).
- [x] OpenAI compat mappings for error.type/code/param.
- [x] Tests: unit + integration + streaming behavior.
- [x] Docs and migration notes.

Migration notes for integrators:
- Clients should stop relying on ad-hoc 429 bodies and prefer the structured envelope: error.type, error.code, error.message, error.retry_after. Retry-After may be seconds (string integer) or HTTP-date. SDKs should support both.
- Where clients used heuristics on connection resets for streams to detect rate-limiting, they should update to expect a final error event on the stream.
- New X-Idempotency-Key header is optional but recommended for any client retries; SDKs will include helpers to generate safe idempotency keys.

Testing & rollout plan:
- Unit tests for middleware and mapping added. Integration tests simulate quota exhaustion and assert Retry-After header and stream final event. Load tests run in perf-canary to verify storage overhead for idempotency records. Gradual rollout: feature flag gated behind runtime config for first week in prod; will be enabled account-wide after monitoring for anomalies.

Files changed (high-level): see changed_files field. For reviewers: I kept changes small in the OpenAI compat layer and centralized logic in pkg/api/errors.go and pkg/api/rate_limit.go to avoid divergent behavior across endpoints.

Related: ENG-1832 (rate-limit semantics), ENG-1920 (idempotency keys), SUP-4567 (customer incident that motivated streaming change).
commits: Add unified rate-limit error family and Retry-After parsing (pkg/api/rate_limit.go)
Introduce X-Idempotency-Key middleware and in-memory store with TTL (pkg/http/middleware_idempotency.go)
OpenAI compat: map internal errors to openai error.type/code, add param/internal_context fields (pkg/openai_compat/response_mapper.go)
Emit structured final error event for streaming endpoints and include Retry-After metadata (pkg/streaming/connection_manager.go)
SDK: expose idempotency helper and handle retry-after variations in python & ts sdks (redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-typescript)
Docs: add docs/api-rate-limits.md and migration notes
review_comments:
Miguel Torres: Can you clarify TTL for idempotency store? We should default to 24h but make configurable per-account.
Asha: TTL is 24h default; added account config hook and comment in middleware. See pkg/storage/idempotency_store.go

Ellen Chu: For streaming final error event, please ensure backpressure codepath doesn't swallow the error when payloads are mid-flight.
Asha: adjusted connection_manager to enqueue final error and drain; added integration test that asserts terminal event is observed.

Ravi Menon: OpenAI compat changes look good but call out that param may be null. SDKs need to guard.
Asha: updated mapping docs and unit tests to include null param case.
release_notes: Standardize rate-limit responses and idempotency semantics: (1) 429 responses include a structured error body and Retry-After header; (2) X-Idempotency-Key supported for idempotent retries (24h TTL default); (3) streaming endpoints emit a final structured error event on rate limit instead of abruptly closing; (4) OpenAI compatibility layer now returns stable error.type and error.code fields. See docs/api-rate-limits.md for migration guidance.
migration_guidance: Handle structured error envelope: error.type / error.code / error.message / error.retry_after
Support Retry-After as an integer (seconds) or as HTTP-date
For streams, expect a terminal error event with type=rate_limit instead of connection reset
Use X-Idempotency-Key for safe retries on mutating requests; SDKs will provide helpers
